subject: Finova: decision criteria — latency, cost, deployment, SLA (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@finova.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call - latency / cost / deployment 

Tom / Sara - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so procurement/security can move forward. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Summary of requirements we heard today:
- Latency: target P95 <= 120ms for 512-token requests in production. Peak tails matter for UX; P99 around 300ms acceptable for background batch workloads.
- Cost: target blended cost goal to keep inference unit economics under ~$0.004 per 1k tokens (to hit current product-level COAs).
- Deployment: preference for Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable latency; evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) if compliance requires network isolation.
- SLA: initial ask 99.9% availability for core inference endpoints, with latency SLOs and 15-min incident response for Sev 1.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and encryption-at-rest keys; procurement will need MSA + DPA redlines.

Requested next steps (proposed timeline):
1) I'll send a concise SLA + deployment options summary and a mutual action plan (MAP) by tomorrow (attachment).
2) Tom/Sara: run the MAP by procurement and security; can you confirm primary procurement contact and timeline?
3) We will provide an initial cost estimate & deployment diagram for Dedicated vs Private by end of week.
4) If you want, we can schedule a short follow-up to review latency targets with engineering (20-30m).

Attachments: redwood-map-sla-summary-20260615.pdf (SLA & deployment options), finova-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP template).

Thanks - I'll follow up with the MAP doc and a dedicated vs private cost sketch.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@finova.com>, procurement@finova.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call - latency / cost / deployment

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency: the 120ms P95 aligns with our consumer app requirement. For our fraud-detection batch jobs, higher latency is fine. Good to see Dedicated as the preferred path.
- Cost: your estimate target looks reasonable; procurement will push back on any upfront committed spend they don't see a clear ROI on.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required. Also need to confirm data retention & audit log access; security will ask for a short questionnaire.

Procurement contact: procurement@finova.com (cc'd) - our lead is Elena Park (procurement@finova.com). Timeline: procurement wants MAP and any contract redlines within two weeks to get to legal review.

We'd like the follow-up latency review with engineering - early next week works. Can you include a rough cost delta between Dedicated and Private (per-month committed cost + expected per-token variable) in the MAP?

- Tom
Tom Reynolds
CTO, Finova

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@finova.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@finova.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call - latency / cost / deployment

Thanks Tom - looping in Rishi (solutions lead) who will join the engineering latency deep-dive and pull the cost estimates together.

Rishi: could you confirm availability for a 30-minute sync on Mon, Jun 22 at 10:00am PT? Agenda: 1) walk through P95/P99 assumptions and expected concurrency; 2) Dedicated vs Private cost delta; 3) required artifacts for procurement/security (SOC 2, retention policy, audit logs).

Tom / Sara / Elena: I attached a MAP with suggested owners and dates. I've also added a short SLA summary in the first tab (availability + latency SLO language) - this is intentionally conservative and we can tighten after technical sync.

If procurement wants a redline-friendly MSA, we can provide a clean MSA and an indexed redlines doc for faster turnaround.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@finova.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery call - latency / cost / deployment

Happy to join the sync - Monday Jun 22 at 10:00am PT works for me. I'll bring:
- A short latency model (P50/P95/P99 projections) based on expected concurrency and 512-token profile, with realistic headroom assumptions.
- Side-by-side cost estimate: Dedicated reserved monthly vs Private one-time setup + per-month ops + per-token variable.
- Checklist for procurement/security: SOC 2 attestation, DPA, KMS options, retention & audit log details.

Marissa - I'll draft the cost slide and paste into the MAP by end of day Friday.

See you Monday.

Rishi
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
